headline: Excretion removes what's harmful or useless—systems that can't eliminate waste eventually poison themselves
universal_truth: Outputs include waste; systems that can't eliminate what they don't need become toxic
fun_facts: Your kidneys filter about 50 gallons of blood daily, producing 1-2 quarts of urine
You exhale about 200 milliliters of water vapor daily—breathing is excretion
Liver failure is fatal within days because toxins accumulate without processing
discussion_questions: What should you be eliminating but aren't?
How do you regularly clear out what's no longer needed?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every living system produces waste—byproducts, toxins, things that don't serve anymore. Without elimination, waste accumulates and poisons. Excretion isn't glamorous, but it's essential. What you remove matters as much as what you keep.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We focus on inputs and outputs but rarely on waste. Yet failed excretion is fatal. What does this teach us about systems?

options.text: Waste removal prevents toxic accumulation—every process creates byproducts; without elimination, useful space gets filled with harmful residue
options.response: Yes. Waste isn't just useless—it becomes harmful if not removed. Elimination is as important as acquisition. Clear the old to make room for the new.

options.text: Waste is just what's left over after using what you need
options.response: True, but without active removal, 'leftover' becomes 'poison'...

q1.title: Active Elimination
q1.script: Excretion isn't passive—it requires energy and systems. Kidneys actively filter blood. Liver processes toxins. Lungs expel CO2. Waste removal is active work, not automatic disappearance.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Active Elimination"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Toxic Accumulation
q2.script: When excretion fails, toxins build up. Kidney failure means waste in blood. Constipation means waste in gut. The timeline varies, but the pattern is consistent: blocked elimination leads to poisoning.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Life Waste
q3.script: Your life accumulates waste too: old commitments, outdated beliefs, draining relationships, physical clutter. Without active elimination, life gets clogged. Regular clearing prevents toxic accumulation.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Outputs include waste. Systems that can't eliminate what they don't need become toxic. Make elimination a regular practice.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 245. Tomorrow, we'll explore going from one cell to trillions—growth. Until then, identify one thing you should eliminate.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Elimination Practice - What Needs to Go?
growTrack.activity: What's accumulated in your life that no longer serves? Commitments, possessions, habits, relationships? Pick one thing to eliminate this week. Regular clearing prevents toxic buildup. Excretion is essential.
